title: Learn Swing Dance! Lindy Hop for Beginners: Charleston Rhythm (Class 1 of 6)

method.teacher_system: The teachers first establish the rhythm and basic groove solo with music, letting learners explore walking around before introducing weight shifts and counts. They then add structure by breaking down slow steps and quick-quick timing separately. Finally, they apply leadership roles and combine the elements together in structured practice rounds.
method.signature: They have built-in practice rounds with music throughout the video, instructing learners not to touch their devices.

practices.what: Start finding the rhythm and walking around with music, choosing any starting foot freely.
Walk forward while keeping the rhythm going, exploring intentional movement.
Walk sideways with an intention that goes forward and back.
Go forward with one foot, then side-to-side, then switch to the other foot.
Count two counts per weight shift, experiencing slow versus quick-quick timing.
Combine two slow steps and a quick-quick rhythm together.

adaptations.adjustment: take the whole class alone and bring those skills to a partner later
just need a little bit of space around you

beliefs.belief: Swing dance has space for freedom, and anyone can express themselves regardless of prior knowledge.
In swing dancing there is no clear rule that you must always be a leader or follower; it is really free.

moments.says: The teacher introduces the beginner lesson and explains that no prior experience or dancing background is expected.
The teacher invites the learner to find the rhythm and move around the room together with the music.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling welcome, capable of moving freely, and ready to explore swing dance without prior experience.
